collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A trader returns a carved staff taken from the village long ago: give it to the family it came from, or keep it where all can see.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A trader has brought back a carved staff that left Isola generations ago. (subject) recognizes the carvings: it belonged to (subject.his/her) great-grandmother's family. (friend) thinks something so old and important should hang in the meeting hut for everyone. What should happen to it?

choices.label: Keep It in the Meeting Hut

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The staff goes to (subject)'s family. (subject) holds it for a long time without saying anything. The family invites the village to see it once a year, at the harvest. Everyone comes.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject)'s family agrees, after a long discussion, to let it hang in the meeting hut, with the family's name carved beside it. (subject) visits it every morning. Some of (subject.his/her) relatives still wish it were home.
